## Problem

Kailash OS is a NixOS-based distribution for AI security work. The
project builds the distribution declaratively from a manifest of 337
tools across four layers. A profile selects the tool categories a
Kailash system carries. The task: pick the profile that matches the
role — red-team, blue-team, ops, or agent infrastructure. The recipe
also shows the selection steps. The checks verify the booted system
matches the requested profile.

## Solution

The image encodes the profile. Choosing a profile IS choosing an
image. Match the role:

| Profile | Carries |
|---|---|
| `minimal` | the CORE substrate — kernel, base userland, hardening, safety defaults, desktop, CLI & menu engines; no tool categories enabled |
| `redteam-ai` | the AI red-team lab scope — ATTACK core plus its OPS/DEFENCE pairings |
| `full` | the complete live catalogue ("kali-everything" lab scope) |
| `headless-agent` | base + CLI only, no desktop; the qcow2 grows at first boot |

On the booted system, confirm the landed CLI surfaces:

```bash
# 1. The profiles the release declares
kailash profile list

# 2. What the manifest carries for your interest area
#    (manifest inventory — every command reads the manifest)
kailash list --layer ATTACK
kailash search prompt-injection

# 3. One tool's full record: ATLAS tactics, OWASP mapping, docs pointer
kailash info garak

# 4. The manifest invariants, locally (the CI gate, runnable by hand)
kailash manifest validate
```

What success looks like:

- `kailash profile list` names the release's declared profiles
- `kailash info garak` returns the full manifest record. The record
  names layer ATTACK, category a-02, and safety `requires-target`. The
  record also carries ATLAS tactics (AML.T0051, AML.T0054), OWASP
  LLM01 for both epochs, and the docs pointer
- `kailash manifest validate` passes. The loader self-inventory is
  green on the installation

## Discussion

- **Declarative, not imperative:** the system configuration enables
  categories. A rebuild is the install step. No imperative package
  action can move the system away from its declaration. A rebuild
  against the same lock reproduces the same tool set exactly — see
  [Enable the first category](first-category.html).
- **`kailash list` shows the manifest, not the boot state:** every
  CLI command reads the manifest. The CLI derivation bakes the
  manifest to a store path. The CLI can never disagree with the
  declared build. What a profile carries is a build-time fact:
  per-category VM tests boot a VM and `--help`-smoke the tool
  list from the manifest. That is the verified instrument, not a
  hand-run command surface. The `kailash doctor`-style per-tool
  installed/version/smoke check is specified but not landed. It lands
  per the roadmap. Track it on the OS repo's CLI lane, not here.
- **Pick `redteam-ai` for the cookbook's attack lanes:** the
  scanning and pair recipes assume ATTACK tooling present. Pick
  `headless-agent` for automation hosts without a desktop.
- **Safety posture comes with the profile:** even on `full`,
  exp-class tools stay behind the [lab-mode gate](../admin/lab-mode-gating.html).
  `requires-target` tools do not self-fire. The profile states the
  tool set. The safety classes govern the run behaviour.
